key_insight: Co-optimizing network topology, dynamic line ratings, and variable impedance devices can reduce grid congestion and operating costs while retaining computational tractability.
engineering_relevance: The framework helps transmission operators coordinate grid-enhancing technologies to better utilize existing infrastructure.
method: Model topology switching with a node-breaker formulation and adjust line limits using weather-dependent ratings.
Jointly optimize discrete topology decisions and variable impedance settings.
Iteratively refine McCormick relaxations of bilinear terms to improve solution accuracy.
evidence_signal: Tests on the IEEE 118-bus system and other benchmarks report better accuracy than standard McCormick relaxation, solution quality close to the nonlinear formulation, and computational efficiency.
watch_item: The abstract provides no numerical accuracy or runtime results, so practical scalability and relaxation error require further assessment.
paper_title: Co-Optimization of Network Topology and Variable Impedance Devices under Dynamic Line Ratings Using Iterative McCormick Relaxation
